operations: Harmony Gold's Bambanani shaft on Klippan 14 farm about 8 km south of Welkom (Matjhabeng), Free State; shaft-pillar extraction on the Basal Reef with ore treated at Harmony One plant. Closed in June 2022, about 18 months early, because of seismicity; ~1,500 staff redeployed; R144m impairment. No longer listed among Harmony's operations on its website (Free State operations now Joel, Masimong, Phoenix, Target 1, Tshepong North, Tshepong South, Central Plant Reclamation). Owner unchanged: Harmony Gold Mining Company Limited (head office Randfontein, +27 11 411 2000).
scale_note: FY2022 (last year): 46,072 oz from 176 kt milled; 1,120 people (1,070 employees + 50 contractors) - miningdataonline; 64,044 oz in FY2021

operations: Harmony Gold underground mine (amalgamated Elandsrand and Deelkraal, bought from AngloGold in 2001) some 90 km west of Johannesburg near Carletonville on the Gauteng-North West border; twin vertical and twin sub-vertical shaft systems mining the Ventersdorp Contact Reef at 3,388 m; ore processed at the Mponeng gold plant. Life-of-mine only 3 years per Harmony's FY25 page. Powered by Eskom. Owner: Harmony Gold Mining Company Limited.
scale_note: FY25: 116,675 oz (3,629 kg) at 6.67 g/t; 3,972 people (3,499 permanent + 473 contractors); energy intensity 0.96 MWh/t treated; LoM 3 years

operations: Harmony Gold deep-level underground mine (acquired from AngloGold Ashanti March 2018) about 10 km east of Orkney and 30 km from Klerksdorp, Klerksdorp goldfield, ~180 km SW of Johannesburg - NOT Carletonville as the DMPR listing had it. Three vertical shaft systems (top mine/Great Noligwa, middle mine, lower mine with the Zaaiplaats growth project), 1,791-3,052 m; ore treated at the Noligwa gold plant. PROVINCE CONTRADICTION: Harmony's website groups it under North West and the town (Orkney) is in North West, but Harmony's SEC technical report summary places the lease south of the Vaal River in the Free State (Moqhaka municipality), and Wikipedia's infobox says Gauteng; coordinates above are from the SEC report. Site of Harmony's Sungazer 2: 100 MW solar PV (three plants) at Moab Khotsong/Great Noligwa, R1.5bn green loan, generation expected from FY2027, EPC OptiPower/Cox Group JV. Grid supply from Eskom. Owner: Harmony Gold Mining Company Limited.
scale_note: FY25: 198,820 oz (6,184 kg) at 8.21 g/t; 6,232 people (5,108 permanent + 1,124 contractors); energy intensity 0.98 MWh/t treated; LoM 19 years incl. Zaaiplaats; FY26 guidance 175,000-178,500 oz; 100 MW solar under construction

operations: Harmony Gold's Mponeng, the deepest mine in the world (3,160-3,740 m), on the West Rand ~15 km from Carletonville (Merafong City), ~65-90 km SW of Johannesburg on the Gauteng-North West border; main shaft with sub-shaft, breast mining on the Ventersdorp Contact Reef, ore treated at the Mponeng gold plant (which also treats Kusasalethu ore). Acquired from AngloGold Ashanti 1 Oct 2020 together with Mine Waste Solutions; life extended by 13 years to ~2044 (2024 approval). Powered by Eskom per the SEC technical report. Owner: Harmony Gold Mining Company Limited.
scale_note: FY25: 333,402 oz (10,370 kg) at 11.27 g/t; AISC R804,429/kg; 6,087 people (4,753 permanent + 1,334 contractors); energy intensity 1.10 MWh/t treated; LoM 19 years; FY25 capex R2,043m

operations: Harmony Gold's Target 1: single-shaft underground mine (mechanised and conventional stoping) at 2,300 m, about 30 km north of Welkom between Allanridge and Odendaalsrus on the R30 (address 20 Buffalo Road, Allanridge), Matjhabeng, Free State; ore milled at the Target plant. operations: Harmony Gold's Tshepong Operations = Tshepong North (1.5 km east of Odendaalsrus, 1,600-2,400 m, Basal Reef with B Reef, ore railed to the Harmony One plant in Welkom) and Tshepong South/formerly Phakisa (between Welkom and Odendaalsrus, 1,500-2,300 m, railveyor to Nyala shaft, ore to Harmony One plant). operations: Buffelsfontein gold mine south of Stilfontein / SE of Klerksdorp (City of Matlosana). Simmer & Jack asset taken over by Village Main Reef in 2011; VMR (owned by China's Heaven-Sent Gold group since 2015) closed it in 2013 as having no viable orebody and the shafts were sealed in 2014 (Buffelsfontein Gold Mines is a discontinued operation in VMR's structure). Since closure the shafts have been worked by illegal miners - the 2024-25 Stilfontein siege/trapped zama zamas happened here. Village Main Reef's websites (villagemainreef.com, villagemainreef.co.za) are dead/lapsed; no current operator page, no published load.
scale_note: Closed 2013; historic reserves 11.02 Moz (Wikipedia). No current production or employees.

operations: Hartebeestfontein ('Harties', 8 shafts, to 2,400 m) near Stilfontein/Klerksdorp; merged with Buffelsfontein in 1999 by DRDGOLD as the North West Operations (Harties = north division, Buffels = south division), later Simmer & Jack, then Village Main Reef (2011). Closed with Buffelsfontein in 2013; Wood Mackenzie lists 'North West Operations (Hartebeestfontein & Buffelsfontein) (Closed)'. Hartebeestfontein Gold Mining Company remains a VMR/Heaven-Sent group entity. No current operator page or load.
scale_note: Closed 2013; no current production or employees

operations: Kopanang (ex-AngloGold Ashanti Vaal Reefs No. 9 shaft), underground gold mine 1,350-2,240 m near Orkney, ~15 km SE of Klerksdorp, ~250 km SW of Johannesburg - the DMPR listing's 'Nala, Free State' is wrong (Kopanang Gold Mining Company is North West). Sold by AngloGold Ashanti to Heaven-Sent SA Sunshine Investment Company (China) in Feb 2018 and run by its South African subsidiary Village Main Reef together with Tau Lekoa and the West Gold Plant. Placed on care and maintenance in March 2020 (Section 189 for 6,309 jobs across Tau Lekoa, Kopanang and West Gold Plant; Kopanang cash losses R305m since 2018); no official restart announced as of July 2026. Village Main Reef's web domains are dead; no current leadership or contact page could be found.
scale_note: Last reported 82,000 oz (2019); 537 kt mined (2018); 6,309 employees across VMR's three operations at the April 2020 s189 notice

operations: Gold One Group's Modder East operation directly north of Springs (Ekurhuleni), 30 km east of Johannesburg, East Rand Basin; shallow underground mine (300-500 m) commissioned 2006, first new East Rand mine in 30 years, mining right ~39.9 km2, with the Gedex mine and rights over Cons Modder/Ventersburg. Gold One is owned by China's Baiyin Nonferrous Metals Group (head office Constantia Office Park, Weltevreden Park, Roodepoort). Oct 2023 underground sit-in of 540 workers. operations: Gold Fields' South Deep, bulk mechanised underground gold mine in the Witwatersrand Basin near Westonaria (Rand West City), ~45-50 km SW of Johannesburg; Old Vereeniging Road, Farm Modderfontein, Westonaria 1780; Twin Shaft and South Shaft complexes, processing plant with tailings retreatment section; 32.19 Moz reserve, LoM to ~2101. operations: Ekapa Minerals / Ekapa Resources (Ekapa Mining), 1 Molyneaux Road, Beaconsfield, Kimberley; Kimberley's last diamond miner - underground Joint Shaft (Dutoitspan/Bultfontein) and Wesselton to ~800 m, the Combined Treatment Plant (CTP) reclaiming ~140 Mt of tailings, and surface mining; bought the CTP and tailings from De Beers in 2016 and Petra's Kimberley interests in 2018; controlling shareholder Marcel Golding. Mud rush on 17 Feb 2026 killed five miners at the lowest level; company filed for liquidation within a week; Northern Cape High Court extended provisional liquidation to 30 Oct 2026; joint provisional liquidators launched a 90-day sale process on 11 May 2026. Now on a structured care-and-maintenance programme (~115 staff, ~R10m/month, continuous pumping, 47 km perimeter). Coordinates are the historic Kimberley Mine (Big Hole) in town, not the CTP.
scale_note: Plant capacity 9.6 Mt/y; ~140 Mt tailings resource; three kimberlite pipes (Du Toits Pan, Bultfontein, Wesselton); ~1,000 jobs affected by the liquidation, ~115 on site (May 2026)
